- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.11 or -0.22 in sentiment history) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.22) — model fails to anticipate downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts toward historical mean too early.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum — especially when sentiment is positive, model delays peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overproject upward trend — correct by reducing slope in later days.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs as sustained — sentiment decay (e.g., -0.22) should trigger downward adjustment in forecast.
- If sentiment is consistently low or negative over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope and add downward bias.
- Model often misses early correction after spikes — correct by adding a 1–2 day lagged correction to forecast.
